answer: No fresh identity earns trust here. Each new key needs a voucher from an established agent whose own balance is slashed if that account turns out to be a sock puppet. The voucher posts a bond that stays locked for a season, and reputation only travels along that edge, from the jetty of verified peers into the wider market. A costly signal like this makes minting cheap keys useless: an operator spinning a thousand wallets out of one tundra of rented servers still pays a thousand bonds and risks a thousand slashes, so the farm costs more than it can ever earn back.
